Failed shift direction sensor on the actuator
Faulty shift lever or selector module where it sends the signal
No up- or downshifts, gearbox keeps the current gear
P2794: P2794 means the shift direction signal, which tells the controller whether a gear is being pushed in or pulled out along its lane, reads lower than the permitted minimum. The usual suspects are a signal line rubbed through to ground, a collapsed sensor supply shared with other sensors, or water in a connector creating a leakage path to ground.
Signal line chafed through to ground
Shared sensor supply pulled down by another sensor or wiring
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
Gearbox stays in the current gear
P2795: P2795 is the upper-limit fault of the shift direction signal: the value seen by the controller is higher than any real sensor position could produce. That pattern fits a signal wire touching a battery or 5 volt feed, a lost sensor ground, or an interrupted signal line on an input that is pulled up inside the module.
Signal wire shorted to battery or 5 V supply
Lost sensor ground or open signal line pulled up internally
Shift direction sensor stuck at a high output
Gear changes refused, current gear held
Selector or paddle inputs have no effect
P2796: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump A Control Circuit/Open

P2796 points to an interrupted control line between the module and the motor of auxiliary pump A. GM's 2025 TCM tables define the test: provided the battery supplies 9 to 15 V, the controller sees more than 200 kΩ from signal to ground in at least 20 of 25 samples taken every 100 ms; the code is Type B, so the MIL comes on after two trips.
Broken control wire or unplugged pump connector
Poor terminal contact at the pump or module
Open circuit inside the pump electronics
Reduced performance message on electrified models
P2797: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump A Performance/Stuck Off

P2797 says pump A was asked to deliver but no useful pressure resulted. GM checks this on CVTs during an engine auto-start: with the pump commanded and over 400 kPa requested at both pulleys, both pressure sensors reading under 200 kPa for more than 0.525 s set the Type B code.
Internal failure of the auxiliary pump or its motor
Control software misjudging pump output (TCM update available)
Low fluid or internal leakage preventing pressure build-up
Shock or surge when the engine restarts at a stop
P2798: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump A Control Circuit Low

P2798 reports the control circuit of auxiliary pump A pulled low, which in practice means a short to ground. In GM's 2025 TCM tables the controller registers less than 0.5 Ω between the signal and controller ground in 20 of 25 samples at a 100 ms rate, with battery voltage between 9 and 15 V; it is a Type B fault with the MIL after two trips.
Control wire chafed through to ground
Internal defect in the pump electronics (e.g. faulty solder joints, Bolt EV/EUV)
Moisture or corrosion bridging pins in the connector
Faulty control output in the module
Reduced propulsion power message on electric vehicles
Service vehicle soon lamp or MIL
P2799: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump A Control Circuit High
P2799 is set when the control line of auxiliary pump A sits at too high a level, normally because it touches a powered wire.
Control wire shorted to a powered circuit
Moisture bridging pins in the pump connector
Internal short in the pump electronics
Faulty high-side driver in the module
P279A: Transfer Case Gear High Incorrect Ratio

P279A fires when the transfer case should be in its high range, but the measured ratio says otherwise. GM explains the check in its 2019 ECM tables (section for the LCV engine): the ratio is calculated from transmission output speed divided by transfer case output speed, both from real sensors.
Range shift to high not completed by the shift motor
Worn shift fork or range sleeve slipping out of high
Implausible transfer case output speed signal
Mismatched tire sizes affecting the computed ratio
Unexpected low-range feel or loss of drive
P279B: Transfer Case Gear Low Incorrect Ratio

P279B is the reverse case of P279A: 4WD low has been commanded, yet the transfer case behaves like high range or neutral. For a vehicle crawling off-road this is a real safety concern, because the expected reduction and engine braking are missing.
Shift motor stopping short of the low position
Worn or damaged reduction planetary set
Broken or bent range shift fork
Faulty speed signal distorting the ratio
No reduction in 4WD low, weak crawling and engine braking
Clunking or grinding when selecting low range
P279C: Transfer Case Gear Neutral Incorrect Ratio

P279C applies when neutral is commanded on the transfer case, as is done for flat towing, but the shafts still turn with a fixed ratio that matches high or low range. The transfer case therefore still transmits drive.
Range shift motor not reaching neutral
Sticking shift sleeve keeping a range engaged
Wrong position feedback from the range sensor
Vehicle still drives or creeps with neutral selected
P279D: Four Wheel Drive (4WD) Range Signal Circuit

P279D concerns the signal that tells the powertrain which transfer case range is active: 4WD high, 4WD low or neutral. Drivetrain controllers need it to apply the right ratio, torque limits and shift logic.
Range message from the transfer case module corrupted or out of sequence
Open circuit or bad connector on the range switch or sensor
Faulty transfer case control module or range sensor
Software mismatch between the modules after a replacement
4WD range indicator wrong, flashing or unavailable
Range change between high and low refused
P279E: Four Wheel Drive (4WD) Range Signal Circuit Range/Performance

P279E flags a 4WD range signal that is electrically present but does not make sense: it may show a range the transfer case cannot be in, jump between high, low and neutral without a request, or contradict what the speed ratio across the transfer case shows.
Worn or misadjusted transfer case range sensor
Transfer case shift motor stopping between ranges
Intermittent contact in the range signal wiring
4WD indicator shows a range that does not match the actual drive
Range shifts refused or completed only partly
P279F: Four Wheel Drive (4WD) Range Signal Circuit Low

P279F means the wired 4WD range signal is below the lowest valid level. Many transfer cases report their range through a resistor-coded switch or a position sensor that produces a defined voltage for each of high, low and neutral; a reading under the lowest of these bands points to a short to ground, a missing sensor supply or a sensor that pulls the line do…
Range signal wire shorted to ground near the transfer case
Range switch or encoder failed with low output
P27A0: Four Wheel Drive (4WD) Range Signal Circuit High
P27A0 is logged when the line reporting which transfer case range is engaged (4WD high, 4WD low, neutral) reads above its highest valid level.
Range signal wire or encoder ground interrupted (corroded or loose connector near the transfer case)
Signal wire chafed against a powered conductor
Transfer case range encoder or switch defective
4WD indicator flashing or showing no range
Shift between 4WD high and low refused
P27A1: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump A Stuck On

P27A1 means auxiliary transmission fluid pump A keeps running although the controller has not asked for it, or the module still sees current or rotation with the command off. Such electric pumps hold pressure in the gearbox while the engine rests during stop-start or hybrid operation.
High-side driver or pump relay stays closed
Pump control or enable line shorted to battery voltage
Integrated pump electronics ignore the off command
Pump hum from the gearbox after the engine or ignition is off
P27A2: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump B Control Circuit/Open

P27A2 flags a broken control circuit between the module and auxiliary pump B, the second electric fluid pump on gearboxes that carry two. While its output is energised, the controller compares the voltage on the line with the level an intact load would pull it to; a floating line reveals the interruption. No manufacturer documents P27A2 publicly.
Control wire broken in the harness to pump B
Pump connector unplugged, pin pushed back or corroded
Open motor winding or internal connection in pump B
Harsh engagement when driving off after a restart
P27A3: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump B Performance/Stuck Off
P27A3 means auxiliary pump B was commanded but did not deliver: no pressure build-up, too little speed or a motor that does not respond at all. Audi documents the code.
Pump B mechanically defective or seized (e.g. assembly fault on Audi V553)
Fluid level too low, pump draws air
Worn pump motor or high resistance in its supply
Rattle from below the car near the gearbox
Delayed or harsh engagement after an engine restart
P27A4: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump B Control Circuit Low

P27A4 indicates that the control line of auxiliary pump B is pulled toward ground. The module checks the line while its driver is switched on; if the measured level stays close to zero, the circuit counts as shorted low. No manufacturer documents P27A4 publicly.
Control wire insulation chafed through to ground
Water or corrosion bridging pins to ground in the pump connector
Internal short to ground inside pump B
MIL or transmission warning after repeated trips
Blown fuse in the pump supply possible
P27A5: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump B Control Circuit High

P27A5 sets when the control line of auxiliary pump B sits at a level that only a connection to a voltage source can explain. In practice the wire touches a powered conductor, or moisture links it to a neighbouring supply pin. No manufacturer documents P27A5 publicly.
Control wire chafed against a powered conductor
Moisture bridging the control pin to a supply pin
Faulty output stage in the controlling module
Pump B may run continuously or not at all
MIL after two trips on Type B systems
P27A6: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump B Stuck On
P27A6 reports that auxiliary pump B keeps running, or keeps drawing current, while the controller has it switched off.
Pump B module or electronics defective (e.g. Audi V553 supplier fault)
Driver output or relay remains closed
Control line shorted to battery voltage
Pump noise or rattle from the gearbox area with the engine off
P27A7: Pressure Control Solenoid A Data Incompatible

P27A7 means the transmission controller holds no usable calibration curve for pressure control solenoid A. Each valve body is measured at the factory, and GM writes its current-to-pressure data into TCM memory; at every start-up the module checks that record.
New or service TCM installed without loading the solenoid characterization data
Valve body replaced but the data for its part number not written to the TCM
Data set for a different solenoid class or valve body entered
Programming aborted, leaving a corrupted block (checksum error)
Harsh engagements or firm shifts from imprecise line pressure
Transmission may run a substitute program
P27A8: Pressure Control Solenoid B Data Incompatible

With P27A8 the TCM rejects the stored characterization record of pressure control solenoid B. GM's 2016 eight-speed table 16OBDG03 ties B to clutch 2 (CB12345R) and logs the code within one trip when that record is marked as not programmed.
Characterization download skipped after TCM or valve body replacement
Data loaded for the wrong valve body part number
TCM non-volatile memory corrupting the stored block
Converter lock-up shudder or no lock-up on the nine-speed
Uneven upshifts involving the affected clutch
P27A9: Pressure Control Solenoid C Data Incompatible

P27A9 concerns solenoid C. GM's controller compares the calibration it holds for this valve with the valve body actually fitted; if the block for C is absent, of the wrong device class, damaged or non-monotonic, the fault is stored at power-up and lights the MIL in that same trip (Type A in 20OBDG04 and in the 2025 table 25OBDG03A).
Replacement TCM fitted without solenoid C data
Valve body or solenoid assembly swapped without updating the TCM
Stored data corrupted, checksum no longer matches
MIL on in the first drive after the fault
Slipping or harsh application of the clutch fed by valve C
On the CVT, unstable line pressure and belt slip risk
P27AA: Pressure Control Solenoid D Data Incompatible
P27AA is set when the TCM finds the calibration block for pressure control solenoid D unusable.
Solenoid data not loaded after a transmission or TCM repair
Used TCM from another vehicle still carrying its old valve body data
Wrong valve body part number used for the download
MIL and stored DTC at key-on
Rough shifts into gears using the clutch behind valve D
P27AB: Pressure Control Solenoid E Data Incompatible
Solenoid E's characterization data failing the TCM's plausibility test produces P27AB.
Valve body serviced without rewriting the solenoid data
Incomplete programming session after TCM replacement
Solenoid class in the data does not match the TCM calibration
Flare or bump on shifts using the clutch behind valve E
On the CVT, irregular torque converter lock-up
P27AC: Pressure Control Solenoid F Data Incompatible

P27AC reports invalid calibration data for pressure control solenoid F. On GM's 2016 eight-speed this is the line pressure solenoid, and the TCM logs the fault in one trip once the data are found unprogrammed.
TCM swapped and solenoid F data never loaded
Remanufactured valve body with a new ID not entered into the TCM
Data block damaged by a voltage drop during programming
Firm or soft shifts throughout when line pressure depends on valve F
P27AD: Pressure Control Solenoid G Data Incompatible
P27AD flags the stored data for pressure control solenoid G as not matching the hardware. GM's 2016 eight-speed table names G the torque converter clutch solenoid and sets the code in one trip.
Solenoid G data missing after TCM programming
Valve body changed without matching data
TCM calibration for a different transmission variant
Converter clutch or range mode problems, depending on transmission
General shift harshness on ten-speed units
P27AE: Pressure Control Solenoid H Data Incompatible

P27AE is the highest letter GM publicly checks for characterization data. It is absent from the 2016 eight-speed table and first appears in 17OBDG04, where H stands for the nine-speed's C6 clutch (C6789) and the ten-speed's torque converter clutch; 20OBDG04 adds mode valve B on CVTs with electronic range select.
Replacement TCM delivered blank and not set up with valve body data
Valve body or solenoid service without data update
Shudder or missing converter lock-up on ten-speed units
Higher fuel consumption if lock-up is suppressed
P27AF: Pressure Control Solenoid J Data Incompatible
No manufacturer documents P27AF publicly. By its wording it would mean that the TCM considers the stored calibration of a ninth pressure control solenoid, letter J, invalid.
Solenoid data not loaded after TCM or valve body replacement
Data set for another valve body variant
Corrupted calibration block in TCM memory
Rough or inconsistent shifts involving the element behind valve J
P27B0: Pressure Control Solenoid K Data Incompatible

P27B0 closes the data-incompatible series with letter K, and no public manufacturer document uses it. It would describe a tenth pressure control solenoid whose calibration record in the transmission controller is missing, mismatched or corrupt.
Valve K data never programmed into a new or used TCM
Valve body ID in the TCM differs from the fitted unit
Software update overwrote or damaged the data block
Shift quality problems on gears using valve K
P27B1: Internal Control Module Transmission Range Select Performance

P27B1 belongs to a family of codes raised by an independent supervision layer in the transmission or powertrain module. That layer repeats key transmission decisions in parallel and flags the main software when both results disagree, as a guard against unintended vehicle motion.
Supervision or main software calibration in the module
Implausible clutch shaft speed or position input
Internal fault in the transmission control module
Restricted gear selection or default gear
P27B2: Internal Control Module Transmission Range Control Performance

P27B2 is set when the monitoring layer cannot confirm that the gearbox is really in the range the main software intends. In GM's 2024 tables for heavy-duty trucks, the TCM checks actual solenoid and pressure switch states with the pattern expected for the range; if they disagree for a full second, the code is logged, lighting the MIL on the first trip.
Module software (Ford fixes by reprogramming, e.g. TSB 25-2362)
Unusual operating sequence such as selecting a gear after remote start without braking
Solenoid or pressure switch state not matching the commanded range
Vehicle stuck in park or will not start
P27B3: Internal Control Module Transmission Gear Select Performance
P27B3 is the monitoring code for the path that turns a chosen gear into actuator commands. In Ford's wording it supervises the actuator manager.
Electrical fault at the selectable one-way clutch actuator (Ford 8/10-speed)
Safety-relevant CAN transmit signal faulty (Ford TR9070)
Certain gears or engine braking functions blocked
P27B4: Internal Control Module Transmission Gear Direction Control Performance

P27B4 concerns the direction in which the vehicle actually moves compared with the selected gear. GM's 2024 heavy-duty TCM tables compare the direction reported by the output speed sensor with the direction implied by solenoid and pressure switch states; disagreement for one second sets the code with MIL on the first trip.
Module software strategy (Ford reprograms PCM or SOBDMC)
Faulty direction information from the output speed sensor
Solenoid or pressure switch reporting a state that does not match the gear
P27B5: Internal Control Module Transmission Gear Ratio Control Performance
P27B5 sets when the supervision software doubts the ratio the transmission is running.
Implausible input, intermediate or output shaft speed signal
Real slip of a clutch producing an unexpected ratio
Transmission held in a fixed gear
P27B6: Internal Control Module Transmission Speed Sensor Performance

P27B6 is the supervision check on the transmission speed signals. GM's 2024 heavy-duty TCM tables work out the output speed that should result from turbine speed and the current gear ratio and set the code, MIL on the first trip, when the raw output speed deviates by 10 or more for at least 10 seconds while output speed is at least 50, the range is not neutr…
Turbine or output speed sensor delivering an implausible signal
Damaged tone wheel or interference on sensor wiring
P27B9: Pressure Control Solenoid N Performance/Stuck Off

P27B9 says pressure control solenoid N does not build hydraulic force when commanded. On dual-clutch gearboxes this letter belongs to the second synchronizer pressure valve: Ford's 2024 summary lists it for SPV2 of the TR9070, and GM's 2023 Corvette table 23OBDG07 calls it shift solenoid 2 hydraulically stuck off.
Valve spool sticking closed from debris or varnish
Low or contaminated transmission fluid reducing supply pressure
Leak in the synchronizer actuator circuit
Mechanically binding shift rod or fork
Certain gears cannot be selected; gear skipping
Substitute mode with reduced gear set
P27BA: Pressure Control Solenoid N Stuck On

P27BA is the opposite fault to P27B9: solenoid N keeps applying pressure when it should be released. GM's dual-clutch table 23OBDG07 (Corvette) describes the effect of a synchronizer valve 2 stuck on as a constant push on one shift rod.
Valve spool stuck open by contamination
Worn solenoid armature not returning to rest
Fluid contaminated with clutch or synchronizer wear particles
Gear clash or grinding on shifts
P27BB: P27BB is a catch-all electrical code for pressure control solenoid N, and no manufacturer documents it publicly.
Solenoid N coil open or shorted
Corroded or loose internal transmission connector
Damaged harness between TCM and transmission
Faulty output driver in the TCM
Gears served by solenoid N unavailable
P27BC: P27BC reports that the signal or response of pressure control solenoid N drops out now and then rather than failing permanently. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; the GM and Ford dual-clutch documents that use solenoid N for the second synchronizer valve (23OBDG07, Ford TR9070 list) only publish its permanent electrical and hydraulic faults.
Loose or spread terminal at solenoid N or TCM
P27BD: Pressure Control Solenoid N Control Circuit/Open

P27BD stands for an open control circuit of solenoid N. GM's 2023 Corvette dual-clutch table 23OBDG07 names the part synchronizer actuation valve 2 and tests it while its low-side output is switched off: the driver chip tries to hold the pin at a small voltage with a tiny current, which only works without a load connected.
Broken control wire between TCM and solenoid
MIL on in the same trip
Gears on the affected shift rod blocked
P27BE: Pressure Control Solenoid N Control Circuit Range/Performance

P27BE means the control circuit of solenoid N is electrically intact but behaves implausibly, for example a measured current that does not follow the command. No manufacturer documents P27BE publicly.
Solenoid N coil resistance out of specification
High resistance at connector or crimp
Unstable supply voltage to the TCM
Slow or incomplete gear engagement on one shift rod
P27BF: Pressure Control Solenoid N Control Circuit Low
P27BF indicates the control line of solenoid N is pulled too low, in practice a short to ground.
Control wire chafed through to ground
Moisture or corrosion bridging the connector
Solenoid winding shorted to its housing
Unintended gear actuation or locked-out gears
P27C0: Pressure Control Solenoid N Control Circuit High
P27C0 reports too high a voltage on the control line of solenoid N, usually a short to battery or to a neighbouring output.
Control wire shorted to a supply voltage
Two solenoid lines shorted together in the harness or connector
Partially shorted solenoid coil drawing wrong current
Damaged output stage in the TCM
Shift rod cannot be actuated; gears missing
Code returns at every start after a shutdown test
P27C1: Pressure Control Solenoid P Performance/Stuck Off

P27C1 is logged when pressure control solenoid P is commanded but the shift rods it serves barely move. Delayed or failed launch in affected gear

Chafed or broken lead between solenoid and TCM

Gears on the affected shift rods unavailable

P27C7: Pressure Control Solenoid P Control Circuit Low

Internal wear of solenoid R armature or seat
Grinding or clunk when changing gears

P27CD: Pressure Control Solenoid R Control Circuit/Open

P27CE: Pressure Control Solenoid R Control Circuit Range/Performance

P27CF: Pressure Control Solenoid R Control Circuit Low

P27D6: Pressure Control Solenoid S Control Circuit Range/Performance

P27D7: Pressure Control Solenoid S Control Circuit Low

Control wire chafed through to ground

P27D8: Pressure Control Solenoid S Control Circuit High

P27D9: Pressure Control Solenoid T Performance/Stuck Off

Abrasion particles from clutch or synchronizer wear

P27DB: P27DB is a catch-all for electrical trouble on solenoid T that does not name the kind of fault. No manufacturer publishes it.
Solenoid T coil open or shorted
Corrosion or poor fit at the gearbox connector
Defective TCM output for solenoid T
P27DC: With P27DC the module reports that solenoid T misbehaved only briefly before working again. No maker has published a description of this code. Ford's TR9070, the only known application of a valve T (selector pilot valve, 2024 overview), is covered by lasting electrical codes and by stuck-on and stuck-off codes, none of them sporadic.
Loose pin in the gearbox connector
Particles briefly holding the valve spool
MIL lights up from time to time
Occasional failed or late gear selection
P27DD: Pressure Control Solenoid T Control Circuit/Open

P27DD tells that the control circuit of solenoid T is open, so no current reaches the coil. Ford's 2024 OBD overview gives this code to open load on the selector pilot valve of the TR9070 dual-clutch transmission; the document lists the fault type only, without limits.
P27DE: Pressure Control Solenoid T Control Circuit Range/Performance
P27DE would be set if the circuit of solenoid T is intact but delivers readings the controller considers implausible. No manufacturer documents the code.
Rising contact resistance at a terminal
Solenoid T resistance drifted from nominal
TCM output no longer regulating current
P27DF: Pressure Control Solenoid T Control Circuit Low

P27DF points to a control line of solenoid T pulled too low. In Ford's 2024 OBD summary it is the shorted-switch fault of the selector pilot valve on the TR9070 dual-clutch gearbox, meaning the switched side of the coil is tied to ground and the valve can be powered permanently. Ford publishes no thresholds.
Damaged insulation letting the wire touch ground
Solenoid T coil shorted to ground
Gears fenced off, shifts limited to some gears
P27E0: Pressure Control Solenoid T Control Circuit High

P27E0 reports a control line of solenoid T sitting too high. Ford's 2024 overview of the TR9070 dual-clutch gearbox uses it for a shorted load on the selector pilot valve, a coil or line bypassed to battery so the driver cannot pull current through the winding. Limits are not stated by Ford.
Control wire shorted to a supply feed
Cross-short to an adjacent valve line
Gears of one rod group lost
P27E1: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump A Pressure Too Low

P27E1 is a hydraulic verdict, not a wiring one: electric auxiliary pump A was running on command, yet the pressure it built stayed below what the module expected. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly.
Worn pump gears or internal leakage inside pump A
Low or aerated transmission fluid, pump draws air
Intake screen of the pump partly blocked by debris
Check valve in the pump circuit not sealing
Jerky or delayed engagement when the engine restarts after a stop
P27E2: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump B Pressure Too Low
P27E2 flags that the second electric pump, B, delivered too little pressure although it was driven. Nobody publishes this code openly.
Pump B worn, motor running but delivering too little
Leaking O-ring or pressure line between pump B and the gearbox
Fluid level too low for pump B to prime
Weak battery or poor ground slowing the pump motor
Stop-start no longer stops the engine
Reduced clutch cooling, power limited when hot
P27E3: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Control Valve Circuit/Open

The control valve named here decides where the oil from the electric auxiliary pump goes. Volkswagen's training book for the 0GC seven-speed DSG shows such a layout: pressure regulator N218 shifts a spring-loaded changeover piston that sends the flow of pump V475 either to the mechatronic unit or to clutch cooling. No maker publishes P27E3 itself.
Broken conductor in the valve control line
Pin backed out or corroded at the gearbox connector
Warning light with stored open-circuit fault
P27E4: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Control Valve Circuit Range/Performance

P27E4 is the plausibility check for the auxiliary pump control valve: the circuit is intact, but its current or its hydraulic effect does not match the command. No manufacturer lists the code publicly, so the logic can only be inferred.
Valve or changeover piston sticking from contaminated fluid
Contact resistance at the connector distorting the current
P27E5: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Control Valve Circuit Low

P27E5 sets when the voltage on the auxiliary pump control valve line is pulled toward ground, typically by chafed insulation touching the case or by a coil shorted internally. No manufacturer documents the code openly.
Control line chafed through and touching ground
Fluid or water in the connector bridging to ground
P27E6: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Control Valve Circuit High

P27E6 means the control valve circuit of the auxiliary pump reads higher than allowed, as if the line were tied to battery voltage. A wire rubbing against a live conductor in the same harness, or a driver stage that no longer switches off, are the classic triggers. The code is not documented by any manufacturer in public.
Control line shorted to a supply wire in the harness
Output stage in the control module stuck on
Corrosion bridging adjacent pins in the connector
Warning light on, possibly further pump codes
P27E7: 'Transmission Range Control' belongs to shift-by-wire, where the selected range travels as an electrical signal instead of a cable. Only channel A is documented in public: Mitsubishi's 2022 manual sets P07E8 when one of eight electric shift sensors in the selector rises above 4.5 V for 2.4 s with the ignition on, and names no fail-safe reaction.
Loose or corroded connector at the electric selector
Broken wire between selector and control module
Sensor inside the selector assembly failed open
Warning about the shift system in the cluster
Some ranges not accepted from the selector
P27E8: Transmission Range Control B Circuit Performance

P27E8 is the plausibility test for range control circuit B: the signal is neither open nor shorted, yet its value makes no sense, for example a level stuck between the valid on and off windows. The title reads Circuit Performance, without Range. No manufacturer publishes the code.
Contact resistance at selector terminals shifting the voltage
Spilled drink or moisture inside the selector
Position sensor in the selector degrading
Displayed range occasionally flickers or lags
P27E9: Transmission Range Control B Circuit Low

P27E9 reports that a line of range control circuit B sits too close to zero volts, pointing to a grounded line or a sensor that pulls its output down. It is not described publicly by any manufacturer.
Harness pinched under the center console, shorted to ground
Sensor supply interrupted, output drops to zero
Shift system warning on the display
Usually no change in how the car drives
P27EA: Transmission Range Control B Circuit High

With P27EA, a signal of range control circuit B reads near the supply voltage, which usually means a short to a power wire or a broken ground return that lets the line float high. No manufacturer documents the B code openly.
Signal line shorted to a supply wire
Sensor ground open, signal floats high
Shift system message in the cluster
P27EB: Transmission Range Control A Position Sensor/Switch Circuit/Open

GM uses this code on automatics with internal electronic range selection (ETRS), where hydraulic mode valves within the valve body set park, reverse, neutral and drive. Mode valve A carries a Hall position sensor.
Signal wire of the mode valve A sensor broken or loose
Hall sensor on mode valve A failing
Damaged internal transmission harness or pass-through connector
MIL on after the first trip
P27EC: Transmission Range Control A Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Range/Performance

P27EC is GM's movement check for mode valve A of its internal range selection: after the TCM commands park, drive or reverse, the position sensor must report the new state within a set delay; the logic also watches line pressure and clutch slip. Both the 2018 nine-speed and 2020 ten-speed tables rate it Type A.
Mode valve A sticking inside the control valve body
No hydraulic pressure from a failed auxiliary pump during auto stop
Mode valve A position sensor reading wrong
Delayed or refused shift into park, drive or reverse
MIL on, stop-start may be disabled
P27ED: Transmission Range Control A Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Low

P27ED tells that the Hall sensor on mode valve A of GM's internal range selection delivers almost no voltage. In both the 2018 9-speed and the 2020 10-speed RWD tables the limit is a raw value under 0.414 V for 0.100 s within 0.163 s, with at least 9 V on the battery; GM itself blames a grounded or interrupted line.
Sensor signal shorted to ground in the internal harness
Hall sensor on mode valve A failed
Shifts out of park slow or blocked
P27EE: Transmission Range Control A Position Sensor/Switch Circuit High

The opposite of P27ED: the position sensor of mode valve A reads higher than any valid state. GM's TCM tables for the T87A nine-speed of 2018 and the rear-drive ten-speed of 2020 set P27EE when the raw signal exceeds 2.538 V for 0.100 s inside a 0.163 s sample, describing it as a short to voltage on the sensor circuit; the MIL comes on at once (Type A).
Sensor signal shorted to a voltage source
Sensor ground open, signal drifts high
MIL on from the first trip
Range changes restricted, possible reduced mode
P27EF: Transmission Range Control B Position Sensor/Switch Circuit/Open

P27EF concerns the second mode valve, B, of GM's internal electronic range selection. Its Hall sensor is expected to sit clearly high or clearly low; GM's 2018 9-speed and 2020 10-speed RWD tables treat a raw value between 1.263 and 1.504 V, held for 0.100 s of a 0.163 s sample, as an illegal level.
Mode valve B sensor signal line interrupted
Hall sensor on mode valve B no longer switching cleanly
Fluid or corrosion at the transmission pass-through connector
Transmission warning, neutral or drive engagement may be restricted
P27F0: Transmission Range Control B Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Range/Performance

P27F0 checks whether mode valve B really moves. In GM's 2020 table for the T87A 10-speed RWD transmission, the TCM expects the valve B sensor to follow commands to park, reverse, neutral high or low, neutral shift and drive within a delay; if the final state is not reached under adequate line pressure, the Type A code sets.
Mode valve B sticking in the valve body
Insufficient line pressure to move the valve
Position sensor B reporting late or wrong state
Delay or refusal when selecting neutral, drive or reverse
MIL on, transmission may enter a protective mode
P27F1: Transmission Range Control B Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Low
P27F1 reports a valve B position signal that has collapsed toward ground in GM's internal range selection.
Valve B sensor line shorted to ground
Sensor supply missing at the internal connector
Hall sensor on mode valve B failed
MIL comes on on the first trip
Neutral or drive engagement slow or blocked
P27F2: Transmission Range Control B Position Sensor/Switch Circuit High

With P27F2 the TCM sees the valve B position sensor above its valid range, which GM interprets as a short to voltage on that circuit. The threshold is 2.538 V, which must persist 0.100 s in a 0.163 s sampling period; GM applies it to internal range selection in the 2018 T87A nine-speed and the 2020 rear-drive ten-speed.
Valve B sensor line shorted to a voltage source
Warning light and stored transmission fault
P27F3: P27F3 reports that the second clutch of a gearbox, usually the clutch on the even-gear side of a dual-clutch unit, has exceeded its permitted temperature, either measured or calculated from slip and load.
Pump in the electric clutch actuator blocked by particles

Insufficient clutch cooling or low or aged fluid

Judder or burning smell when pulling away
P27F4: Gear Shift Lock Solenoid/Actuator A Performance/Stuck On

P27F4 concerns the mechanical result of the shift lock, not its wiring: actuator A was commanded but stays in its active state or does not reach the requested position. Whether active means locked or released depends on the design. No manufacturer documents P27F4 publicly.
Lock pin or actuator binding in the shifter mechanism

Implausible brake pedal signal keeping the lock commanded

With P27F5 the control unit concludes that shift lock actuator A remains in its passive state although it was told to act. Depending on the design, that can leave the lever free to leave Park without the brake, which defeats the brake interlock, or permanently blocked. No maker publishes this code.
Loose or badly crimped terminal at the lock solenoid
Weak solenoid coil that no longer moves the lock pin
Broken return spring or worn lock pin
Shifter module software misjudging the actuator position
Selector leaves Park without the brake pedal being pressed

P2800: Transmission Range Sensor B Circuit (PRNDL Input)

P2800 is the general circuit code for the second signal path that tells the modules which selector position (P, R, N, D, L) is engaged. It applies when that signal is unusable without a clear low, high or frequency pattern.

Engine does not start in Park or Neutral
P2801: Transmission Range Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
Here the B signal of the range sensor is electrically present but its content does not make sense.
Range sensor electronics producing a wrong signal frequency

Warning lamp with shift quality or gear display issues
Transmission uses a fixed substitute range strategy
P2802: Transmission Range Sensor B Circuit Low
P2802 means the B signal of the range sensor sits too low, usually a ground short or a duty cycle collapsing toward zero.
Signal wire of sensor B shorted to ground
Water or corrosion in a connector of the circuit
Range sensor output stage failed low
No start in Park, missing gear indication
P2803: Transmission Range Sensor B Circuit High

P2803 is stored when the output of range sensor B reads too high, which typically points to an open circuit or a short to supply voltage. In GM's 2020 and 2025 tables the engine module watches its own range sensor input for this: either under 0.5 ohm to the voltage source or above 200 kilohms to ground for 0.5 s sets a Type A fault.

Shift system warning in the instrument cluster

P2804 points to a B signal that drops out or jumps for short moments instead of failing permanently. Ford is the main user: its 2024 OBD summary books it as the general electrical fault of TRS B (UDS P2800_01), checked continuously, with up to 30 s allowed for pattern recognition and 2 s for analog faults.
Connector not fully seated or pin pushed back
Harness chafing that opens the circuit under vibration
Worn contacts or electronics inside the range sensor
MIL comes and goes, often with several transmission codes

Wrench lamp, gear display differs from lever position
Start refused in Park or Neutral

Debris or wear particles jamming the valve

P2808: Pressure Control Solenoid G Performance/Stuck Off

P2808 means valve G does not deliver the pressure or effect it is commanded to give. GM documents two very different applications. P280B: Transmission Range Sensor B Circuit Not Learned

P280B flags missing or invalid adaptation values for the second range sensor signal. On paper P2813 is a plausibility fault in the control circuit of solenoid G, but its main real-world use is hydraulic. Nissan-built CVTs label it as the select solenoid, which applies the forward and reverse clutches.
